summary: Researched the target user for Momentum (AI habit tracker that adapts to natural energy patterns). Found a large, growing market ($1.3B in 2026, 15% CAGR) with massive churn (92% fail within 60 days). Identified 3 core pain points: rigid streak punishment, one-size-fits-all scheduling ignoring energy variability, and feature overload. Defined 2 personas (Overwhelmed Olivia, age 28-35, and Optimizing Owen, age 25-38). Mapped platform breakdown: Reddit (primary, 1.1B users, productivity subreddits with 2M+ members), TikTok (primary discovery, 1.59B users), LinkedIn (secondary, 1.1B), Indie Hackers (niche high-conversion). Energy-adaptive habit tracking is a genuine white space — no major competitor leads with this positioning.

key_findings: Habit tracker market is $1.32B in 2026, growing at 15.18% CAGR, with 61% of US adults having tried a habit app
92% of habit tracking attempts fail within 60 days; 22% abandon apps within first 30 days
AI is the #1 differentiator users seek — 36% of habit apps now use ML, AI-driven recommendations improve completion by 22%
Energy-based adaptive habit tracking is a genuine market gap — no major competitor leads with this
'Streak shame' is the #1 emotional pain point driving abandonment across all sources
Millennials are the heaviest AI users (24% daily usage) — prime demographic for Momentum
Productivity app users skew 25-40, educated, higher-income, tech-savvy

personas.name: Overwhelmed Olivia
personas.core_frustration: Energy and motivation vary day to day; apps assume consistency

personas.name: Optimizing Owen
personas.core_frustration: Wants data correlations between habits and performance; current trackers only show streaks

pain_points.evidence: Dominant complaint across Reddit (multiple threads, hundreds of upvotes), Medium articles, and market analysis
Reddit users explicitly cite 'unpredictable energy levels' as #1 reason for failure; competitor Tracka.ai now positioning on this gap
22% uninstall within 30 days; notification overload drives 16% of uninstalls; users report 'overloaded UI' as quit reason
